title: Working Set
description:
CoALA working memory for one decision cycle: the goal in play, what was retrieved into it, and what has been observed so far.

This is deliberately NOT durable knowledge. It is a short-lived scratch buffer that exists so a loop can survive a crash, so a trajectory can be reconstructed, and so runaway loops can be detected. It expires. Anything worth keeping has to be promoted into a long-term record by memory_remember or memory_close_cycle.

The working set is the memory agent's, not the host's: it does not attempt to own or mirror the host's context window.

parent_cycle_id.description: Set when this cycle runs inside another agent's cycle, e.g. a subagent in a fan-out.

goal.description: What the host is trying to achieve this cycle, in its own words.

loop_signature.description: Stable hash of the normalised goal plus the first action taken. Two cycles with the same signature and no change in outcome are the definition of a stuck loop; this field is what makes that detectable cheaply.

status.description: 'abandoned' is set by the daemon when it reaps a cycle that was opened and never closed — an unclosed cycle is evidence of a crash, not something to discard.

expires_at.description: TTL for the scratch buffer itself. Default 24h. Expiry destroys the working set, never the episodic records promoted out of it.

retrieved.description: Records pulled into working memory this cycle. `injected` distinguishes what was actually handed to the host from what was merely a candidate, so recall quality can be evaluated after the fact.

observations.description: Append-only log of what happened this cycle, written before the host acts on each result. On close these become episodic records; on abandonment they are still promoted, marked outcome='abandoned'.
